To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of a few graphene layers in alumina powder results in a decrease of the grain size, a significant increase in the electrical properties, and a moderate increase of the indentation fracture toughness.
graphene addition to alumina by chemical vapour depositions leads to a dramatic increase in fracture toughness, hardness and electrical conductivity.
the addition of 1 wt.% of graphene to Al2O3 resulted in a 13 order of magnitude increase of the electrical conductivity and in 40% decrease in fracture strength.

the synthesis and characterisation of conductive aluminate composites manufactured by spark plasma sintering from graphenated alumina powders.
the effect of the graphene addition on the microstructure and mechanical properties of alumina composites.
the synthesis of graphene-coated Al2O 3 powders, their consolidation by spark plasma sintering, and the effect of the content of graphene on the microstructure of the compacts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of graphene layers in Al2O3 matrix, even at a very low concentration, has a significant influence on the mechanical behaviour of the composite, and the presence of graphene is also responsible for a remarkable increase of the electrical conductivity.
the presence of graphene in Al2O3 matrix significantly improves fracture toughness and conductivity, while slightly decreasing elastic modulus and hardness.
the addition of graphene to alumina matrix results in a significant increase of fracture toughness and electrical conductivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
graphene can be a good candidate to enhance the electrical and mechanical properties of Al2O3 ceramics.
graphene addition to Al2O3 matrix by SPS resulted in a decrease of the Al2O2 grain size and an increase of the electrical conductivity, hardness and fracture toughness.

we have demonstrated that SPS is an efficient method for the production of conductive aluminate based composites, and that graphene is a promising material to improve the mechanical properties of aluminate based compositse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SPS process is a suitable method for manufacturing of conductive alumia/graphene composites, and that the addition of graphene improves mechanical properties of alumina.
the addition of graphene to alumina powders by chemical vapour depositions results in composites with improved fracture toughness and electrical properties.
the SPS process can be successfully used for the fabrication of conductive aluminas, and that a small graphene content is enough to achieve high electrical conductivity.
